Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of that same problem. To prevent the function from running forever, you must provide a simple base case where it stops and returns an answer. Imagine looking up a word in a dictionary, only to find that the definition uses another word you do not know, forcing you to look up that new word too. You keep doing this until you hit a word you already understand, and then you can finally trace your steps back to understand the original word.
